top_choice_rationale: P004 credits a concept of molecular organisation: biomolecules demix into liquid-like condensed phases governed by valency, affinity and saturation concentration, shown in living cells (P-granules, Hyman and Brangwynne) and in a defined in vitro system (Rosen). The thermodynamic framework is independently reproduced and extended across many fields, and the narrowed citation (general physical-chemical principle, organizing biomolecules in cells) does not claim every condensate is an equilibrium phase or functionally essential. I accept that it is less mature than P001 and that Pappu and Mittag are left out by the three-name cap, so P001, with a one-principle induced-proximity citation, is my clear second choice, followed by P003 (narrow reversible-terminator chemistry), P002 (mature but closest to the 2010 prize and needing careful handling of Kosugi), and no award last.
recusal_note: My research on lipid and protein self-assembly is scientifically close to the P004 field (and to ionizable lipid nanoparticles, not on this slate); no personal or institutional tie to any credited laureate. Lund colleagues Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai are an institutional overlap, not a recusal ground.
